newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs end limit down, pork bellies down sharply.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs end limit down, pork bellies down sharply.

text.p: Pummeled by active fund long liquidation and lack of commercial support, October CME hog futures ended down the 1.500-cent-per-lb daily limit and other months finished sharply lower on sell stops.
Pork bellies also ended down sharply on fund selling and sell stops, traders said.
October hogs closed limit down at 58.125 cents per lb with other months off mostly 1.525 to 0.675 cent with 2.000-cent-limit lean contracts off most.
Pork bellies were down the 3.000-cent limit in May earlier but futures ended 2.900 to 1.800 cents lower, paced by February at 74.600 cents.

After starting to look technically weak Thursday, hog futures tumbled from the start Friday as funds liquidated long positions and sell stops took prices sharply lower. A midsession rally on short covering lacked follow through and prices fell to new day's lows and limit losses when fund selling continued, traders said.

Futures became overbought Wednesday and started a break that met only thin support, partly reflecting concern over weakening pork prices and a seasonal break that usually starts around October 12, they said.

"The twelfth starts a seasonal down - but just like the Labor Day break everybody said we were going to have this year -- we had it a week early," said Dave Butterfield, market analyst for Rand Financials.
Butterfield said the market already looked technically weak with large open interest and commercials were unwilling to buy in the face of a seasonal downtrend.
The heavy pace of hog slaughter this week weighed on pork belly futures and that market also fell sharply as prices ran into technical fund stops shortly after the opening.
Sell stops started at 76.800 cents, basis February, and increased under 76.000 cents.
"We have everything going against the market," one trader said.
In hog options, Refco actively bought December 59 calls late. Lind-Waldock bought December 54 puts early. Volatility was firmer in February and April and steady in December, pit sources said.
